In CSS nesting, writing `:hover` directly inside an element's block without the ampersand (`&`) acts as a descendant selector (`& :hover`) rather than targeting the element itself. Since `root>mid>leaf` is a leaf node with no children, this selector matches nothing, which is why adding `:hover { padding: 40px }` inside its CSS block changes nothing. To fix this and apply the hover state to the element itself, you must edit `root>mid>leaf`'s own CSS block to use `&:hover`.

ANSWER: root>mid>leaf
